subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.
reasoning:
I'm sketching out a chibi axolotl design with a stubby body, feathery gill fronds, big smiling eyes, and a pale pink spotted body, then planning the skeleton hierarchy starting from the hip joint for posing the limbs and tail.

Working out the spine, head, and tail joint positions and sizes to keep proportions chibi-like, with a leaf-shaped tail fin plate extruded in a vertical plane, then moving on to sizing the stub legs attached to the body sides.

Now I'm defining the joint hierarchy: hips as root, a spine chain leading to the head joint, a jaw joint positioned and aimed separately from the head for the mouth, with upper snout parts mounted on the head bone and lower jaw parts on the jaw bone, and I'm about to work out eye placement next.

For the eyes, I'm going with small dark spheres positioned on the upper sides of the head with tiny white highlight spheres for a cute chibi look, and considering adding blush decals on the head surface using a radial gradient, targeting the head part as the decal surface.

For the mouth, I'm using a smile-shaped SVG decal projected onto the curved front of the head, plus two tiny dark spheres for nostrils. For the gills, I'm planning three stalks per side rooted behind the head, swept outward and curved upward with tapered radius and darker pink coloring, then adding frond details along each stalk using card decals.

Working out fanned gill endpoints and curved bezier sweeps with tapered round caps, plus tip spheres, before moving to gill bone joint chains.

Now I'm planning to use two-joint chains per gill as the sweep source for each fin, then setting up front leg joints (shoulder, elbow, hand) as a simple polyline chain for the limb geometry.

For the rear legs I'm placing hip, knee, and ankle joints parented to the hips, then sweeping with a tapering radius. For the hands I'm adding finger spikes fanning outward from the tip joint, using directional offsets to spread them naturally around the hand frame.

Still writing finger geometry...

For the body, I'm considering sweeping the spine and tail together as one continuous path from tail tip to head, bound to the full bone chain so the transitions stay seamless.

Still writing radius function...

Adding countershading with mottled spots, deeper pink for the gills, and scattering tiny freckle-like marks across the back for texture. Now I'm sketching the tail fin outline, extruding a shape along the z-axis near the hip to form a flattened fin profile.

Still shaping the fin outline...

Now I'm moving to the head, planning a scaled sphere geometry to form its basic rounded shape.

For the lower jaw, I'm sizing and positioning a smaller flattened sphere colored like the belly, attaching it to a jaw bone with a joint that opens downward and forward. I'm also placing a smile decal on the lower front of the head, figuring out the hit position and direction so it sits naturally on the snout.

For the eyes, I'm computing the surface position on the head ellipsoid at a given side offset so the eye sphere embeds correctly, then adding a black pupil sphere and a small white highlight offset toward the upper-front for a glossy look.

Now I'm placing tiny nostril spheres by solving for their position on the front surface of the head ellipsoid, then adding a blush decal computed similarly on the side surface for a cute chibi effect.

For texture, I'm sticking with three decals (frond pattern, smile, blush), then moving to code: building frames from a sweep along a bezier chain for each gill, naming the joints systematically, and setting the frond flow direction to point outward and slightly downward by default.

Then I'm working out the fingers -- adding a pink pad sphere at each fingertip bone, positioning finger base joints relative to the tip with small offsets, and using thin capsules in a flat belly-pink tone for the finger segments.
